chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan, from Ja'far ibn Sam'ah, from Aban, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who transfers a debt to another man (makes a third-party transfer of debt/hawalah); does the original debtor return to the creditor? He said: 'He does not return to him ever, unless he had gone bankrupt before that.'

key_terms.أَفْلَسَ: went bankrupt / became insolvent of insolvency

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Hawalah (debt transfer) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permanence of debt release in Hawalah, emphasizing that the original debtor remains discharged unless insolvency occurred prior to the transfer. This ruling underscores the principle of finality in financial transactions within Shia fiqh, distinguishing between mere non-payment and legal bankruptcy (aflasa). It provides jurists with a clear criterion for determining when a debtor's liability reverts to them, ensuring clarity in commercial contracts.
